questions.question: Chromatography is highly versatile. What are the two main purposes for which chromatography can be used?
options: Separation of large-scale bulk materials and chemical storage
Separation of minute samples and analysis of substances
Measuring boiling points and determining density of solids
Increasing the solubility of gases and creating saturated solutions

questions.question: If a scientist runs a chromatography test on a sample and it is a completely pure substance, how many spots will be produced on the chromatogram?
options: Only one spot
At least two spots
A continuous streak of spots
No spots at all

questions.question: What would you expect to see on a chromatogram if the sample being tested is a mixture of several different dyes?
options: No spots will appear on the paper
Only a single, large black spot
Many spots at different heights
The paper will dissolve completely

questions.question: Why is pencil, rather than ink, used to draw the starting line on chromatography paper?
options: Pencil is insoluble in water and will not run with the solvent
Pencil graphite reacts chemically with the paper to stay in place
Ink would evaporate too quickly before the process begins
Pencil is magnetic and aligns the chromatography paper

questions.question: Under what conditions is simple distillation typically used to separate a mixture?
options: When separating a mixture that contains only two substances
When separating a mixture with four or more different gases
When the substances in the mixture have identical boiling points
When separating insoluble sand from a salt solution

questions.question: Which technique is best suited to separate a mixture that contains three or more liquid substances, or substances with very similar boiling points?
options: Simple filtration
Decanting
Fractional distillation
Paper chromatography

questions.question: During distillation, what happens if the condenser warms up instead of remaining cold?
options: It becomes more effective and speeds up the collection of distillate
It becomes less effective and more gas will escape without condensing
It will cause the flask to freeze and crack
It makes the liquid boil at a much lower temperature

questions.question: What is the process called when a solute reforms as crystals from a saturated solution following a change in conditions?
options: Simple distillation
Crystallisation
Decanting
Chromatography

questions.question: Under what conditions do larger crystals form during the crystallisation process?
options: When the solvent is boiled away rapidly
When the solvent evaporates more slowly
When the mixture is shaken vigorously while hot
When the solvent is frozen instantly

questions.question: Which of the following materials can be directly separated from a dry mixture using a magnet?
options: Iron and steel
Copper and aluminium
Sand and salt
Gold and silver

questions.question: How can insoluble solids be successfully separated from a liquid?
options: By using a filter in a process known as filtration
By performing simple distillation to boil the solid
By using a separating funnel to let the solid float
By using paper chromatography to dissolve the solid

questions.question: What is the characteristic behavior of immiscible liquids when they are mixed and allowed to settle?
options: They dissolve into each other completely to form a single phase
They react chemically and turn into a solid precipitate
They do not mix, and one liquid will float above the other
They instantly evaporate into the surrounding air

questions.question: How can the boiling points of liquids be used to separate miscible liquids?
options: By freezing them until one becomes magnetic
By changing their physical states through heating and cooling
By filtering them through fine filter paper under pressure
By using a separating funnel to drain the denser liquid

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of steps required to separate pure salt from rock salt?
options: Evaporation, chromatography, and decanting
Simple distillation, magnetic separation, and fractional distillation
Making a solution, filtration, and crystallisation
Fractional distillation, decanting, and filtration

questions.question: Why should a condenser be kept cold during the process of distillation?
options: To speed up the condensation of the vapor back into liquid
To prevent the glass from melting due to the hot liquid
To slow down the rate at which the mixture in the flask boils
To allow the solid crystals to grow larger in the collection beaker
